children: Smartphone retailers are scrambling to find second-hand mobile vendors ahead of the festive season as customers look for alternatives amid mounting prices.

Tired of waiting out the growing component costs, many customers have started asking retailers about second-hand mobiles. The demand has reached a point where retailers at a recent Bajaj Finserv event were exchanging contact details of refurbished-phone vendors to buy the products in bulk, according to Kailash Lakhyani, Founder and Chairman of the All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA).

“Until last year, there was no such demand. So, vendors selling second-hand devices were few and far between. Samsung and Vivo offer refurbished products directly through their websites and service outlets, while Cashify has its own outlets across India,” said Lakhyani. He added that sales of new smartphones in mainline stores have dropped by 30-40 per cent since Independence Day, driven by a continuous month-on-month surge in smartphone prices.

Meanwhile, the soaring demand for refurbished devices has created a supply gap in the market, prompting the Organised Retailers Association (ORA) to schedule a meeting with key players such as Cashify in Chennai on September 22 to better understand this emerging trend.

When approached, Nakul Kumar, Co-founder and CMO of Cashify, said there is healthy consumer interest ahead of the festive season for refurbished smartphones, particularly in the ₹20,000-₹45,000 price range.

“Demand is increasingly being driven by consumers seeking premium features and 5G devices at more accessible prices. New launches and festive offers also accelerate upgrade cycles. As existing users sell their devices, the secondary market benefits from better supply, wider choice, and stronger demand,” said Kumar, pointing to a market shift from an affordability-led proposition to a value-led alternative for aspirational buyers.

Accordingly, retailers are now offering buyback programmes, purchasing old phones, refurbishing them, and reselling them. Lakhyani estimated that demand for refurbished phones could grow manifold, as brands may no longer be able to offer 5G smartphones priced below ₹20,000 amid the ongoing price surge. While this presents a significant business opportunity, the trend is also pushing consumers who cannot afford new devices, or who want flagship specifications on a limited budget, towards refurbished models.

Counterpoint Research has also noted the growing relevance of refurbished smartphones for this year’s festive season, with strong volume growth in the refurbished segment during H1 2026. Rising new smartphone prices are making premium refurbished devices more attractive to value-conscious consumers.

“The festive period could further support this trend, as higher exchange and upgrade activity brings more recent models into the secondary market,” said Shubham Singh, Tech Analyst at Counterpoint Research. He added that refurbished smartphones would continue to complement, rather than replace, the new smartphone market. Trust, warranty, battery health, and financing options are likely to be key factors determining how much of the festive demand ultimately converts into sales.

As smartphone prices rise, loans and EMIs are also becoming more difficult to access, according to Cashify’s latest white paper. Stricter lending norms and higher rejection rates mean many consumers, especially those with limited or no credit history, cannot easily finance a new device. This makes refurbished smartphones, trade-ins, and upgrade programmes increasingly important as affordable pathways to owning better devices, the report said.

For businesses such as Bajaj Finserv, which assist customers with EMIs for refurbished phones, the trend could create a significant opportunity. Cashify estimates that the pre-owned smartphone financing market could witness 164 per cent year-on-year growth, with the market size expanding from ₹2.6 crore in 2026 to ₹4.3 crore by 2030.

title: Refurbished phones gain traction as new smartphone sales slow
